title: 441 - Metal Storm
method: claude-code: written from the transcript, links verified by script

items.name: Metal Storm
items.description: The episode's game: a 1991 NES action platformer where a mech flips gravity to walk on ceilings.

links.label: Metal Storm - The Cutting Room Floor

items.name: Gundam
items.description: The giant-robot anime franchise that the mech on the box art recalls.

items.name: Irem
items.description: The publisher of Metal Storm, also known for R-Type.

links.label: Wikipedia: Irem
links.note: Japanese video game and pachinko company

items.name: Pluto
items.description: Where the story's defense station with a giant laser sits.

links.label: Wikipedia: Pluto
links.note: Largest dwarf planet in the Solar System

items.name: Alderaan
items.description: The Star Wars planet destroyed by the Death Star, compared to the laser destroying Neptune.

items.name: Magician
items.description: The previous week's NES game, contrasted with this game's gimmick-driven design.

items.name: VVVVVV
items.description: The indie platformer in which you flip gravity instead of jumping, compared with this game.

items.name: Parallax scrolling
items.description: The layered-background effect where layers scroll at different speeds, which this game pulls off with a custom chip.

items.name: Mode 7
items.description: The Super NES graphics mode the parallax effect is compared to.

links.label: Wikipedia: Mode 7
links.note: Graphics mode on the Super NES video game console

items.name: Super Nintendo Entertainment System
items.description: The console whose Mode 7 effects the parallax is compared to.

items.name: Memory management controller
items.description: The custom mapper chip in the cartridge, plus bank switching, that makes the parallax possible.

items.name: Nintendo Power
items.description: The magazine that put the game on the cover of issue 22 with a 12-page strategy guide.

links.label: Wikipedia: Nintendo Power
links.note: American video game magazine and podcast (1988–2012)

items.name: R-Type
items.description: Irem's shooter franchise, whose ship cameos in a background of this game.

items.description: Cited as the model for this game's second quest after you beat it.

links.label: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda (video game)

items.name: Samus Aran
items.description: The Metroid hero, compared for a damaging spinning move similar to the game's gravity power-up.

items.name: Computer and Video Games
items.description: The British magazine that gave the game a score of 88.

items.name: Mean Machines
items.description: A British video game magazine named in the reception rundown.

items.name: IGN
items.description: The games site that ranked Metal Storm 46th on its list of best NES games.

items.name: Limited Run Games
items.description: The publisher that co-released the 2019 Metal Storm reissue.

items.name: Bowser

items.name: Super Mario 3D World
items.description: The Wii U Mario game whose final boss is Meowser.
